ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against French, EU, UN, and OFAC PEP and sanctions lists; compliance with AMF and ACPR AML/CFT guidelines

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L. 210-1 et seq. and L. 227-1 to L. 227-27 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Decree No. 84-406, Articles R. 123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); Order No. 2021-1189 on the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), transmitting the incorporation file to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and the single electronic corporate formation declaration (dossier unique de création) submitted at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS (Article L. 227-2 of the Code de commerce); cash contributions must be released to at least 50% upon subscription, with the balance due within five years; the released funds must be blocked in escrow with a French credit institution or a notaire (attestation de dépôt des fonds) until RCS registration is certified by the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND OF THE PRÉSIDENT OF THE SAS — 1. The draft Articles of Association are adopted without amendment. 2. The share capital is fixed at EUR [●], divided into [●] ordinary shares; each subscriber subscribes and releases, by transfer to the blocked capital account, the statutory minimum of 50% of cash contributions, the balance to be released within five years. 3. The registered office is fixed at [address], France. 4. [Name] is appointed as Président of the Company. 5. The Président is authorized to publish the legal notice, to complete and file the registration dossier with the Guichet Unique, and to take every action ancillary to incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association and appointment of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders, optionally assisted by a notaire (mandatory only for contributions of real property); the beneficial-owner declaration is ultimately registered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutes specifying the SAS legal form, corporate name, duration of 99 years, registered office, share capital, representation, and governance; execute the statutes in writing (sous seing privé) or by notarial deed where in-kind real-property contributions exist; obtain the signature of each shareholder and of the appointed President; prepare the beneficial-owner declaration (RBE) in parallel.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of each shareholder and of the President
Statement or extract of criminal record (bulletin n° 3) for legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a statutory clause is queried, execute a corrective addendum (avenant) and re-sign; the RBE declaration may be completed or corrected at the filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the share capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or a notaire acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the SAS en formation; each subscriber wires the minimum statutory release of 50% of his cash contribution with the subscriber's name as payment reference; obtain the depositary certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) indicating the subscribers and the sums released; the funds remain blocked until the Kbis extract is obtained.
required_dossiers: Order or mandate to open the blocked account
List of subscribers with the amounts released
Anti-money-laundering KYC documentation of the company in formation and of subscribers
Wire transfer confirmations (SWIFT MT103 or bank receipts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further due diligence, provide enhanced UBO and source-of-funds evidence; alternatively deposit the funds with a notaire; if a subscriber defaults, collect the shortfall or reduce the share capital by amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) of the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formation notice stating the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, duration, trade purpose and the names of the legal representatives; after insertion, collect the attestation de parution; perform the publication before submitting the file to the Guichet Unique.
required_dossiers: Draft legal notice (projet d'avis) supplied to the JAL
Extract of the signed Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requires adjustments, publish a corrective rectificatif at the company's cost and obtain a revised attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, transmitting to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic SAS formation form on the national portal; upload the certified statutes, the deposit certificate, the JAL publication attestation, proof of registered-office address, identity documents and the RBE declaration; discharge the statutory RCS fee online; the greffe verifies the legality of the file and registers the company in the RCS within five working days of receipt of a complete dossier.
required_dossiers: Electronic single formation declaration (dossier unique de création)
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate)
Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
Proof of the registered office (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Identity and criminal-record documents of the legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues an incompleteness notice, the applicant has 15 days to supply the missing items; if the deadline is missed, the file is deemed abandoned and a new filing, with a renewed capital deposit certificate, may be required; erroneous registry entries may be corrected by a request for rectification under Article R. 123-104 of the Code de commerce.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), acting through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); online professional portal at impots.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity creating a French SAS obtains its statutory identity through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (guichet-entreprises.fr), which registers the company with the registre du commerce et des sociétés and issues SIREN/SIRET numbers. For VAT purposes, a non-resident taxable person without a French establishment must file a specific VAT identification request with the SIE of the place where the first taxable transaction occurs, providing constitutional documents, proof of foreign registration, description of planned supplies, and expected effective starting date of activity; after validation, the DGFIP issues a French intra-Community VAT number in the form FR followed by 11 characters. A foreign entity established only for intra-EU distance sales may instead register under the OSS (One Stop Shop) regime for EU-wide VAT obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) at entity level. A newly created small SAS may, under restricted statutory conditions, elect for personal income tax (Impôt sur le Revenu) for a transitional period; a French parent holding at least 95% of a French subsidiary may elect fiscal integration under Article 223 A of the French General Tax Code. France does not apply a check-the-box regime; anti-hybrid rules adopted under ATAD restrict classification mismatches and disallow deduction/non-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA, Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general mandatory VAT registration threshold applies to foreign taxable persons making taxable supplies in France: registration is required from the first euro of taxable turnover. For small domestic undertakings, the franchise en base de TVA threshold is €91,900 for goods and €36,800 for services; a reduced threshold applies to certain professional services. For intra-EU distance sales by non-established sellers, the annual cross-border threshold is €10,000, above which registration in the destination Member State or OSS becomes mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing for all B2B transactions on a phased basis: large enterprises from 1 September 2026 and SMEs/micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027. E-invoicing must use structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) transmitted through a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the central PPF (Plateforme Pivot de Facturation) managed by DGFIP. Cross-border transactions are covered by e-reporting obligations. There is no physical VAT stamping; transmission and data validation are electronic and API-based.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating under Article 262 of the French General Tax Code applies to goods dispatched or transported out of the European Union by or on behalf of the supplier, provided the exporter retains proof of physical departure and the transfer of ownership. Services directly linked to exported goods, and certain offshore services, may also be zero-rated if the recipient is established outside the EU. The zero-rating is excluded if the exporter acts for a customer established in France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU – Document Administratif Unique, electronic export declaration)
Commercial invoice issued by the French SAS
Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, or Air Waybill evidencing transportation
Proof of physical departure from EU territory (customs exit confirmation or electronic transit record)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence confirming collection of export proceeds
Customer declaration, contract, or purchase order confirming delivery outside France
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The zero-rating is audited strictly by DGFIP and French Customs. If the export evidence bundle is incomplete, fraudulent, or contradicted by payment flows, the tax administration reassesses VAT at 20% with late-payment interest (0.20% per month), and applies graduated penalties depending on fault: 10% for simple omission, 40% for bad faith, and 80% where the taxpayer is proven to have acted fraudulently or used illicit arrangements. Additional penalties may include a €750 fine per irregular invoice, administrative sanctions, and criminal exposure under Article 1741 of the General Tax Code including fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the authority of the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy; foreign exchange controls are administered by the French Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a member of the Eurozone; the Euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls on capital movements, profit remittances, or dividends for non-resident investors, subject to compliance with EU anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) regulations. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but must be supported by audited financial statements and proper corporate resolutions. The only hurdles are standard tax withholding (if applicable) and documentary requirements for bank transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds in France. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency earnings in foreign currency accounts or convert them to Euros at their discretion. However, all cross-border transactions must be reported to the Banque de France for statistical purposes (via the 'Balance of Payments' reporting system) if they exceed €12,500 per transaction. No conversion ratio is imposed; the Euro is the legal tender and all domestic settlements must be in Euro.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) and Capital Escrow Account (Compte de Séquestre)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE Group (Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Épargne)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) under the EU PSD2 directive, but they are subject to strict licensing by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., those licensed in Lithuania or the UK) can operate in France under passporting rights, but they often face higher scrutiny for corporate accounts, especially for B2B equipment manufacturers. They are viable for ancillary services (e.g., FX conversion, payment processing) but not recommended as primary treasury accounts due to limited credit facilities and potential regulatory friction. Legal constraints include mandatory registration with the ACPR and compliance with French AML/CTF laws.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SAS, physical presence of the legal representative (Président) is generally required for initial account opening at tier-1 banks, especially for capital escrow accounts. Remote opening is possible for operational accounts if the bank offers a fully digital onboarding process, but this is rare for non-resident directors. The ACPR requires enhanced due diligence for non-resident entities; therefore, a physical meeting or a video conference with a notarized power of attorney is typically mandated. For capital escrow accounts, physical presence is almost always required to verify the identity of the beneficial owner and sign the escrow agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity (e.g., non-resident shareholders, layered corporate structure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed corporate structure chart, certified copies of incorporation documents, register of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), and a legal opinion from a French attorney confirming the chain of ownership and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., shareholders from non-EU countries with weak AML regimes)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit enhanced due diligence documentation: audited financial statements of the parent company, bank references from the shareholder's primary bank, proof of legitimate business activity, and a detailed business plan for the French entity. Additionally, provide a sworn affidavit from the beneficial owner explaining the source of wealth and funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., large initial capital injection from a third-party lender)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a comprehensive funding package including loan agreements, promissory notes, and evidence of the lender's regulatory status. Provide a board resolution authorizing the capital injection and a cash flow forecast demonstrating the business purpose. Engage a certified public accountant to issue a comfort letter on the transaction's legitimacy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent KYC documentation (e.g., missing proof of address for directors)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarized copies of passports, recent utility bills or bank statements (within 3 months), and a certificate of residence from the local consulate. If the director is a legal entity, provide the entity's registration extract and a list of its directors with their own KYC documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with a clear purpose code. For France, the purpose code for capital contribution is 'P01' (Investment in equity) or 'P02' (Loans to subsidiaries) under the Banque de France's balance of payments classification. The transfer must include the beneficiary's IBAN (FR76 + 27 digits) and the legal entity name. Verification: The bank will require a copy of the shareholders' resolution, the capital increase deed (if applicable), and the registration with the French Trade and Companies Register (RCS). For escrow accounts, the bank may require a notarized escrow agreement. All transfers must be reported to the Banque de France if exceeding €12,500.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For international trade, the primary rails are SWIFT MT103 (for direct wire transfers) and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700. For high-value equipment sales, LCs are recommended to mitigate counterparty risk. The disbursement process must include: (1) verification of the underlying commercial invoice and shipping documents (Bill of Lading, packing list, certificate of origin), (2) compliance with EU export control regulations (dual-use goods if applicable), and (3) adherence to the bank's anti-money laundering screening. For payments to suppliers, use MT103 with purpose codes such as 'P301' (Trade credit) or 'P302' (Advance payment).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Forward Contracts (FX Forwards) – permitted for hedging commercial exposures up to 12 months, subject to underlying transaction documentation.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permissible for currencies with limited convertibility, but rarely used for Euro-based operations; must be executed through a licensed bank.
Currency Swaps (FX Swaps) – allowed for managing liquidity and rolling over short-term positions, subject to ACPR and ECB regulations.
Options (FX Options) – permitted for hedging contingent exposures, but require advanced risk management approval from the bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with financial statement package (Liasse Fiscale, including balance sheet, P&L, and attachments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service Direction des impôts des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal-year ending 31 December, electronic filing by 18 May of the following year (non-electronic filing by 3 May); generally due within 3 months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax, increased to 40% if not filed after a formal assessment notice; monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% accrues after a 60-day grace period; criminal fine of up to €10,000 in aggravated cases. Registrational strike-off risk arises if tax declarations are absent for two consecutive years, initiating formal notice before the commercial court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing and related corporate deeds at the Commercial Register (Dépôt des comptes annuels au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, including the statement of allocation of profits and auditor’s report if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, deadline is 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to €1,500 for late or non-filing per warning; a judge may issue an injunction requiring filing within one month, with an additional fine of up to €4,500 plus €1,500 per month of continued delay; persistent non-compliance for three years triggers a written notice prior to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification and update declaration of beneficial owners (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) at the commercial registry; update mandatory upon any change in ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the occurrence of any change in beneficial ownership; in absence of change, no annual re-filing is required, and the existing declaration is deemed current at the annual accounts filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the declaration incurs a fine per the French Monetary and Financial Code: €500 per individual for non-natural persons? for a société: €2,000, doubled to €4,000 for legal persons; the company is also exposed to suspension of voting rights and management remuneration, and the RCS data remains legally non-compliant until correction, which may block any subsequent registration or attestation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory for SAS if it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet > €4,000,000; net turnover > €8,000,000; average permanent workforce > 50 employees. An audit may also be required due to group relations, statutory surveillants, or if the company controls or is controlled by a company already subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général - PCG) under the French Commercial Code; IFRS mandatory only for consolidated financial statements of listed companies or entities designated as public-interest entities; individual annual accounts of an SAS must follow PCG.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose an annual standalone UBO re-filing; instead, the Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs stored at the RCS is continuously current. The SAS must file an update with the Greffe within 30 days of any transfer of shares, change in control, or change in qualifying ownership. The annual filing of the statutory accounts serves as a compliance checkpoint; at that moment the company must verify that the RCS UBO record is accurate, and if outdated, immediately file a corrective update to avoid sanctions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Actionnaires / Registre des Compagnies)
Register of Share Transfer Movements (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Minute Book (Registre des Décisions de l'Associé Unique ou Procès-Verbaux d'Assemblées)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs (turnover < EUR 10 million); Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; Tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for groups.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2050-2059) filed electronically via the EFI (Echange de Formulaires Informatisés) portal on impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December: second business day after 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends: within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after adjustments (reported on Form 2058-A)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a permanent establishment in France must report French-source income; otherwise file a limited return if subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward amount to be offset against current year profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from French PE can be carried forward indefinitely but limited to EUR 1 million plus 50% of excess per year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., CIR, CII) and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim CIR if they have a French PE and perform R&D in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies to all companies subject to corporate income tax in France, including non-residents with a PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due (increased to 40% if not filed within 30 days of a formal notice); interest at 0.20% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties for failure to file electronically.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the non-resident beneficiary must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and complete Form 5000 (or 5001 for individuals) to the French paying agent before payment. For EU/EEA parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive may exempt withholding if the parent holds at least 10% of the subsidiary for 2 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 33.33%, interest 33.33% (subject to treaty reductions, e.g., 0% for interest under many treaties, 0% for royalties under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if conditions met).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million (turnover or balance sheet total) for the entity or group; below this threshold, simplified documentation (Form 2257) may be required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the OECD BEPS principles and domestic anti-abuse rules (e.g., Article 155-A, 57 of the French Tax Code). While no formal ESR regime exists, the 'substance over form' doctrine and the principal purpose test (PPT) under DTAs require genuine economic activity, personnel, and risk management in France to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 CGI); additional penalties of 80% of tax evaded (majoration pour manœuvres frauduleuses).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for corporate tax debts if they have personally participated in the evasion; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a French entity without real economic substance (no employees, no premises, no business activity) to claim treaty benefits or avoid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, 40% penalty for lack of substance, and potential criminal prosecution for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid taxes and penalties if the corporate veil is pierced; possible imprisonment for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls (e.g., KYC, transaction monitoring) or facilitating money laundering through the corporate structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 1 million for companies (Article 465-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code); criminal penalties for directors up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable for AML breaches; civil restitution and prohibition from managing a company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for fiber laser cutting machines or related services that deviate from arm's length, shifting profits to low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for serious mispricing, and interest; potential double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's length pricing may be personally liable for penalties and face criminal charges for tax evasion.
